newsitem.title: FRANCE: At least 29 journalists murdered in 1996-watchdog.
newsitem.headline: At least 29 journalists murdered in 1996-watchdog.

text.p: At least 29 journalists were murdered in 1996 because of their work, the press freedom watchdog Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Borders) said on Friday.
The figure was lower than in the last few years as no journalist was killed in previously bloody conflicts such as the Bosnian war or the Rwanda genocide.

Algeria remained the most dangerous country, with eight journalists assassinated, but the number of casualties had dropped three-fold from 1995. The murders were often claimed by armed Islamic groups, the watchdog said.
It said four journalists were murdered in Russia.
"These assassinations, committed on all continents, have one common point: the murderers are still at large. It is likely that most of the crimes will never be punished," RsF said.
RsF said the statistics covered only journalists who were deliberately slain.
The Brussels-based International Federation of Journalists (IFJ) says at least 50 journalists were killed on assignment in 1996.
Russia's Glasnost Defence Fund human rights watchdog says 24 journalists were killed this year in Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) alone.
